integrations.name: Git provider (issue linking)
integrations.purpose: Link tasks to commits, branches, and pull requests; surface CI/commit status on the linked task; optionally auto-transition a task's state when a linked PR merges.

provenance.notes: Plane's db/models/integration/github.py (GithubRepository/GithubRepositorySync/GithubIssueSync) implements the commit/PR-linking side. OpenProject documents and ships separate GitHub and GitLab integrations (docs/system-admin-guide/integrations/github-integration, gitlab-integration) each configured with a webhook secret, an independent second implementation. CI/build-status specifically is only documented at the docs level (not verified in a data model in either source), so it is stated here as part of this integration's purpose rather than as a separate, evidenced integration.

integrations.name: Chat notifications
integrations.purpose: Push task/comment notifications into a team chat channel.

provenance.notes: Plane's db/models/integration/slack.py; single source. No second implementation of a dedicated chat-notification model was found among the other inspected tools (most rely on the generic outbound-webhook mechanism instead -- see public_api_webhooks).

integrations.name: Public API and outbound webhooks
integrations.purpose: A REST API (commonly OAuth 2.0-authenticated) for third-party access, plus configurable outbound webhooks that POST a signed payload to an external URL when chosen events occur (task created/updated, comment added, etc.), so other systems can react without polling.

provenance.notes: Three independent implementations of outbound webhooks: Plane's Webhook/WebhookLog model (per-workspace URL, secret key, per-resource-type toggles, full request/response logging), Vikunja's Webhook model (target URL, a registered event list, HMAC-SHA256 signing, optional Basic Auth), and OpenProject's dedicated `webhooks` module (with an outgoing-deliveries log UI). OAuth 2.0 (RFC 6749) is cited for the API-authentication half; OpenProject additionally ships its own OAuth applications/clients for API access, corroborating that specific pairing.

integrations.name: Calendar sync
integrations.purpose: Expose tasks with due dates (and milestones) as calendar events, via a subscribable feed or two-way CalDAV sync, so deadlines show up alongside a user's other calendar events.
examples: Google Calendar (via CalDAV or an ICS subscription)

provenance.notes: Vikunja ships a real CalDAV server (pkg/caldav: discovery, CRUD, client-compatibility tests against real CalDAV clients) implementing RFC 4791, the authoritative CalDAV standard. Single implementation among the inspected tools, but backed directly by the authoritative protocol specification it implements.

integrations.name: Importer / migration from another tracker
integrations.purpose: One-time import of projects, tasks, and their metadata from another issue tracker or a spreadsheet, used when a team switches tools.

provenance.notes: Plane's Importer model supports GitHub and Jira as source services with a queued/processing/completed/failed status. Vikunja's pkg/modules/migration package ships real importers for Trello, Todoist, TickTick, Wekan, Planka, Microsoft To Do, and CSV, plus its own file-based export/import format -- a considerably broader, independently-built second implementation of the same concept.
